58:1: The selected text explicitly introduces the third parable, concerning both the righteous and the chosen. Neither the ordinal nor either group is omitted.
58:2: The address is directly to you, righteous and chosen ones. Glorious retains the source adjective for their portion rather than silently changing the statement into a prediction.
58:3: The selected text distinguishes light of the sun from light of everlasting life. It then denies an end to their days of life and a count of days to the holy ones. The last holy-ones clause is retained rather than clipped or folded into the previous noun.
58:4: The first clause seeks light but finds righteousness; these are not silently made the same noun. The closing title is Lord of the world, whereas the preceding title is Lord of Spirits.
58:5: The whole unit continues onto the next page. Portion of faith preserves the selected words without adding a lottery or a previously unmentioned recipient. The source says the light has risen like the sun and darkness has passed away.
58:6: The first denial concerns light that cannot be counted, followed by a denial of a limit measured in days. The darkness verb is from asking or examination, not another occurrence of passed away. The two following light-standing clauses are both retained.
59:1: The selected text names both lightnings and lights, and their judgment. The paired purposes are blessing and curse; the curse is not softened or removed. These are the source’s images, not a modern physical explanation of lightning.
59:2: Not ready for publication: the selected dwelling-places expression is daggered and the following thunder-voice phrase is bracketed. Charles printed103 note23 discusses an underlying Greek corruption and proposes judgment-related alternatives, but this proposal adopts none. The provisional English retains dwellings and the bracketed voice instead of silently repairing the connection.
59:3: The revelation is passive, shown to me. The closing flash is for blessing and abundance; abundance is not replaced with the curse from the preceding verse.
60:1: The selected date is the five-hundredth year, seventh month and fourteenth day, in Enoch’s life. Charles printed103 note39 discusses the name Enoch as an editorial replacement for Noah, but this proposal retains the actual selected name and does not adopt that conjecture. The multiplied myriad expressions are retained as large-number expressions, not converted into a modern population total.
60:2: This complete unit crosses onto the next page. The throne is the throne of his glory, and those standing around him include both angels and righteous ones. Head of Days is retained as a source title without inserting a later personal identification.
60:3: The source gives the narrator’s bodily collapse: trembling, fear, afflicted loins and loosening of his whole being, ending with falling on his face. The wording is not changed into an unprinted diagnosis or a calm bow.
60:4: Michael is the named sender of another angel from among the holy ones. The following raising clause and returned spirit are retained, but the pronoun is not expanded into a new named agent. The narrator explicitly says he could not bear the sight.
60:5: The selected statement describes mercy and slowness to anger toward those dwelling on dry land. The repeated relative construction is smoothed into English without changing the recipient group or adding a new date for judgment.
60:6: The selected source negates bowing to righteous judgment, includes denial of that judgment, and says taking his name in vain. The final selected nouns are oath for the chosen and inquiry for sinners; they are not replaced by a different promise. Four printed dots after the final sentence are represented by an ellipsis. Charles’s note on printed104 says verse25 should follow immediately, but this proposal keeps the printed unit order and does not invent a connecting conclusion.
60:7: The selected past-tense separation of two great beasts and the female designation of Leviathan are retained. The source says that day; it is not silently made a new prophecy in the future or a reference to the day of judgment. Depths of the sea follows the abyss/deep noun, not an identification with an ordinary animal species.
60:8: Not ready for publication: the proper-name spelling provisionally represented as Dundayin and the beast’s taking-possession with its breast remain uncertain in this author proposal. The following genealogy really says my forefather, seventh from Adam; it is not changed to a named Noah or an imported different number. No familiar English place-name spelling certifies the printed glyphs.
60:9: Not ready for publication: the power, two beasts, one day, and sea-versus-dry-wilderness contrast can be read, but the exact selected sea-depth word and abbreviated conjunction require further glyph/construal review. The English sea-depth phrase remains provisional; no parallel text or later English edition has been substituted.
60:10: Son of man is an address to the narrator here. The selected text says that he seeks hidden knowledge; it does not supply a personal identification or an additional answer in this unit.
60:11: The selected unit begins with the other companion angel speaking and showing first and last, then continues across the page through heights, beneath dry land, the deep, heaven’s ends and heaven’s foundation. It does not repeat the prior answer or add a modern layered-universe diagram.
60:12: Not ready for publication: the springs/counting, wind-strength and moon/righteousness-force clauses have not been securely connected. The source prints a small parenthetic (le) element in the comparison phrase, which is retained in the source transcription. The repeated divisions are not removed or replaced with a familiar system of heavenly weights.
60:13: Not ready for publication: the relation between falling thunder, division, lightning and their troops remains uncertain. Each selected element is represented provisionally; the English does not certify a reconstructed atmospheric mechanism or an adopted Greek reading.
60:14: Not ready for publication: the sequence of negatives and the starred from-it expression remain insecure as a connected sentence. Resting places and voice are retained, but the draft does not justify dropping a negative or silently supplying from-each-other as an emendation.
60:15: Not ready for publication: the selected treasury/count/sand wording and the distributive bridling clauses remain difficult. The entire cross-page unit is present, including wind, bridle, return, force and the earth’s circuit. No fluent countless-storehouses wording has been imported to replace the selected sand/count phrase.
60:16: Not ready for publication: male sea-wind and a bridle are explicit, but the connected strength-and-returning construction is not securely understood. The draft does not add a destination in the sea or an unprinted instruction to an angel. The final driven/scattered action and all mountains are retained.
60:17: The two selected clauses call the wind of frost its own angel and the wind of hail a good angel. These are kept as stated rather than turning angel into a modern natural-force explanation or omitting the good adjective.
60:18: Rime is the frozen-dew/frost noun supported by Dillmann1865 col79 with an explicit60:18 citation. The final cold term is separately named. Smoke describes the rising appearance; it is not an instruction to call all three terms snow. The source’s wind/angel imagery is not replaced with a scientific cause.
60:19: Not ready for publication: the source explicitly says the wind of mist does not join their storehouses and has its own storehouse. The short form after glory and the relation to light, darkness and seasons are uncertain. The provisional English must not be treated as a certified silent repair. The final source calls its storehouse an angel.
60:20: The selected text locates dew’s dwelling at heaven’s ends and pairs it with rain’s storehouses. The rain and mist clouds join and give to one another. Winter and summer are retained without adding a regional meteorological calendar.
60:21: Not ready for publication pending independent critical review: the selected print ends with four dots, and Charles printed107 note42 explicitly says the sentence’s apodosis, its completing main clause, is lost. The English translates the extant conditional fragment and labels its missing conclusion instead of inventing one. That label is modern explanation, not ancient wording and not a claim that the ancient book was deliberately left unfinished. No complete manuscript survey is claimed.
60:22: The source explains rain as nourishment from the Most High in heaven for those dwelling on dry land and gives rain a measure. The angels receive it; the selected verb is not silently changed to the opposite direction of transfer.
60:23: The selected boundary is as far as the garden of the righteous. This single unit contains no added description of that garden or a new journey into it.
60:24: Not ready for publication: six printed dots follow the providing-food verb, and the following punishment clause is square-bracketed. Charles printed108 note22 identifies the bracketed passage as a repetition from verse25 with a missing word. This proposal keeps the bracketed text visible in the source and provisional English; it does not silently delete it, supply a recipient of food, or borrow a verb from a later English translation.
60:25: The printed square-bracketed when-punishment-rests clause is retained in English as a bracketed repetition. Charles printed108 note31 treats it as a possible repetition but also discusses whether it could introduce the following clause. No unbracketed reconstruction is adopted. The text explicitly includes children with mothers and children with fathers, the not-in-vain denial, and mercy and patience in the final judgment statement.
61:1: The selected text has long cords, wings, flying, and a journey northward. It does not say how many angels there were. The passive giving and their taking wings are retained without introducing an unprinted named giver.
61:2: The question and answer continue across the page. The question is why the cords were taken, and the answer is that they went to measure. No measurement result is supplied in this unit.
61:3: Both the measures and bonds of the righteous are selected nouns; bonds is not silently omitted. The ending is leaning upon the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever, preserving the explicit name and title.
61:4: Not ready for publication: the selected first clause has measuring and chosen dwelling with chosen. The relations of subjects, the following measures-for-faith clause and the righteousness object remain provisional. The draft does not silently replace dwelling with judging or make the measures an imported restoration of a building.
61:5: The lost people in wilderness, those eaten by wild beasts and those eaten by sea fish are all retained. Return and leaning are distinct verbs. Both final denials of perishing remain; the source is not changed into a claim that the listed deaths never occurred.
61:6: The recipients are all those in the height of heaven. Command, power, voice and fire-like light are separately retained; the light comparison is not made a new angel’s personal name.
61:7: First voice follows the selected prior/first expression. Wisdom, speech and spirit of life are all retained; no extra speaker is named.
61:8: The Lord of Spirits seats the chosen one; the next judging action belongs to that enthroned figure. The selected objects explicitly include works of the holy ones, not a silent replacement with sinners. Weighing in the balance remains the text’s judgment image.
61:9: Not ready for publication: the tracks and righteous-judgment continuation and the speech verb are not confidently connected. The draft does not add an unprinted one-voice numeral here, a new judging agent, or a repaired Greek clause. The following blessing, praise, exaltation and sanctification sequence is complete.
61:10: The selected opening verb is transitive call. Charles printed110 note34 discusses a possible underlying Greek mistake, but this proposal does not adopt a joy/rejoicing emendation. The entire unit continues onto the next page through cherubim, seraphim, ophanim, angels of power and dominions, chosen ones, and the other host on dry land and water.
61:11: The selected source explicitly has one voice twice. Faith, wisdom, patience, mercy, judgment and peace, and goodness are retained in order. The blessed-name formula and everlasting conclusion are not clipped.
61:12: The source distinguishes those who do not sleep, the holy ones, the chosen in the garden of life and every spirit of light. The relative light-spirit phrase is a capacity expression, can, not a new negative. The bracketed relative before beyond-its-strength is kept in the source. The shift from him to your blessed name is retained rather than normalized throughout to third person.
61:13: The selected text says rich in mercy and slow to anger, then all work and every measure he made. The revelation is to the righteous and the chosen. No fresh personal identification or unprinted scope of creation is inserted.
